name: Censer
overview: The censer was a sacred vessel used in the Old Testament for offering incense before the LORD, symbolizing the prayers and worship of His people. Specifically, it was made of gold for use in the temple (Numbers 4:14) and played a central role in the Day of Atonement service, as seen when the high priest took a censer full of burning coals and incense into the holy place (Leviticus 16:12). The censers used by Korah and his followers in their rebellion were commanded by God to be transformed into plates as a sign of judgment (Numbers 16:6-7, 16-17). While censers were employed in idolatrous rites, their primary biblical significance is symbolic, pointing to the holiness required before God and the acceptance of worship offered in faith.
